No borrow script, scen28 scenario or battery ran on these nine this cycle. The builds match what cycle 28 recorded, so nothing is known to have regressed, but nothing new was tested either.

BNB Chain Jenner and Polygon Salvador and Tempo T14 fall on 8 December 2026, 11 days after this cycle. No cycle 29 unit held lens L5 or L6 (every unit's lenses were L1 to L4 in plan.json), and the open high leads L-1032, L-1075, L-1076 and L-545 that hold the day-one reruns are still unassigned. Jenner and T14 were rehearsed under block-time overrides in earlier cycles (cleared items for chain 56 with block time 1796697600 and chain 4217 with 1796745600). Salvador never was: no cleared item runs battery.py or targeted.py on Polygon under a block number override at or past 98,688,600, and the public endpoint runs a private bor build (bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private) whose fork table nobody has read.

The consensus path of Monad (native code from the gcc 15.2.0 emitter in the shipped validator package) is still untested by any harness. theme-monad-gcc-register-spill left L-1167 inconclusive ('The gcc emitter's register, spill and stack offset logic was not run'), theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds cleared only the literal arms, and high-throughput did not rerun the native engine (L-1172 inconclusive, 'the cycle 28 harness was not rebuilt'). rpc.monad.xyz runs only the interpreter, so every RPC result this cycle describes the interpreter.

theme-tempo-binary-keccak-transient lifted KECCAK256 from both v1.19.1 binaries (L-1169 cleared) but not SLOAD, SSTORE, TSTORE or the journal rollback loop. The verifier added that evm2's take_transient_storage(address) exists and was not tied to its call sites in the shipped binary. The source reading (cleared item 'Every non-test caller of ... take_transient_storage in the Tempo workspace at a9d6748') says none runs while a user transaction is on the stack, so this is a binary-level gap only.

stablecoin-l1 found three public Arc endpoints each serving one build (v0.8.6-rc1 at 37812c61 and v0.8.6 at 8e8edb7a, both unpublished, and the v0.8.5 tag at 602eed3b), but which build the validators run is still unknown, and no keyless endpoint serves traces (L-1096 inconclusive). Arc is a native-face network (F-032, F-108, F-050), so its value-call hook is in the settlement path.

The two closed producers still rest on replicas. MegaETH's sequencer build is closed (L-1144 inconclusive) and the below-range borrow of getFeeGrowthInside (src/libraries/Pool.sol:499-500) has never been executed by it in the 3,000,000 blocks checked (L-1152 inconclusive). HyperEVM had no unit; its validator is closed and its headers carry a zero state root (F-120), so the public clients never check its storage writes.

leads.question: Build one x86 model run of the gcc 15.2.0 emitter's register and stack bookkeeping in the shipped Monad 0.16.7 package (alloc_general_reg 0x36ae40, alloc_or_release_general_reg 0x36b020 and 0x39a300, alloc_avx_reg 0x36aa80, write_to_final_stack_offsets 0x3816e0, block_prologue 0x392cd0) with the _emitI recorder of cycles/029/theme-monad-gcc-literal-folds.work/scripts/emdrv.py. Feed it the Stack states the clang harness logs at entry of the 49 deepest PoolManager blocks and of the blocks that hold FullMath.mulDiv (src/libraries/FullMath.sol), SqrtPriceMath.getNextSqrtPriceFromAmount0RoundingUp and SwapMath.computeSwapStep. Does the emitted instruction stream equal the clang listing up to register renaming, and does any destination register alias a live operand?
leads.why: Validators certify state from this native code, while every public RPC result, trace and battery run comes from the interpreter. A gcc-only register or spill fault in a block on the swap path would give the network a different price or amount word than the source, which a swapper who finds the stack shape could repeat against any pool. Merges L-1167 and the two medium leads of this cycle.

leads.question: Does the Polygon endpoint's private build bor/cb3d19c5f690/v2.11.1-private carry the Salvador block and the MULMOD memo? Send eth_call with blockOverrides number set to 98,688,600 and to 98,688,601 and check whether the five Salvador target accounts' rules or any rule-dependent probe change; if Salvador is active under the override, run battery.py and targeted.py under that override now.

leads.question: Run scripts/fgi_census.py of cycles/029/high-throughput.work on MegaETH from block 7,009,653 to 29,942,333 and on Monad's PoolManager over its whole history: give the first block where each borrow of getFeeGrowthInside (src/libraries/Pool.sol:499-508) occurred in a mined transaction, and whether the producer's stored fee growth words equal the source there.
leads.why: These are the two producers that run code no public endpoint runs (MegaETH's closed sequencer, Monad's gcc native code). A mined word that differs from the source on an unchecked wrap is the cheapest evidence of a producer-only fault in fee accounting, which would move fees between LPs.

leads.question: Pick 50 recent HyperEVM blocks with PoolManager activity. For every storage slot those transactions wrote (from a prestateTracer diff on a nanoreth replica), does eth_getStorageAt on rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm at the same block equal the replica? Report the first slot that differs, or zero differences.
leads.why: HyperEVM headers carry a zero state root (F-120) and the validator is closed, so no client checks its storage writes. The last comparison was 8,867 items at one block. A validator-only arithmetic or storage fault would be the network's truth and an ordinary swapper could use it.

leads.question: In both tempo v1.19.1 binaries, which call sites reach evm2 State::take_transient_storage and the SSTORE, SLOAD and TSTORE host routines, and does the lifted control flow show take_transient_storage running only after the outermost frame has returned, as the source reading at a9d6748 says?
leads.why: If any call site ran while a user transaction was on the stack, the PoolManager's lock flag, NonzeroDeltaCount and CurrencyDelta slots (src/libraries/CurrencyDelta.sol:21-39, src/PoolManager.sol:104-114) could be emptied mid-unlock, which would let a caller close an unlock with debt erased. Source says no; the shipped binary was not checked.

leads.question: Under Rex4 per-frame budgets on MegaETH, what exact status and return data does a frame give when it exceeds its budget: is it always success = 0, or can it ever end with success and empty return data? Test with eth_call on a contract that exhausts the per-frame data and kv budgets inside a CALL and reports the call's success flag and returndatasize.
leads.why: Currency.transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:66-76) counts a call that returns no data as a successful ERC-20 transfer. A budget stop that ended with success and no data would let take debit nothing real while the caller's delta is closed. The unit read it as a revert from documentation only.
